rape-of-lucrece-l703: Drunken Desire must vomit his receipt,
rape-of-lucrece-l704: Ere he can see his own abomination.
rape-of-lucrece-l705: While Lust is in his pride, no exclamation
rape-of-lucrece-l706: Can curb his heat or rein his rash desire,
rape-of-lucrece-l707: Till like a jade Self-will himself doth tire.
rape-of-lucrece-l708: And then with lank and lean discolour’d cheek,
rape-of-lucrece-l709: With heavy eye, knit brow, and strengthless pace,
rape-of-lucrece-l710: Feeble Desire, all recreant, poor, and meek,
rape-of-lucrece-l711: Like to a bankrupt beggar wails his case:
rape-of-lucrece-l712: The flesh being proud, Desire doth fight with Grace,
rape-of-lucrece-l713: For there it revels; and when that decays,
rape-of-lucrece-l714: The guilty rebel for remission prays.
rape-of-lucrece-l715: So fares it with this faultful lord of Rome,
rape-of-lucrece-l716: Who this accomplishment so hotly chased;
rape-of-lucrece-l717: For now against himself he sounds this doom,
rape-of-lucrece-l718: That through the length of times he stands disgraced:
rape-of-lucrece-l719: Besides, his soul’s fair temple is defaced;
rape-of-lucrece-l720: To whose weak ruins muster troops of cares,
rape-of-lucrece-l721: To ask the spotted princess how she fares.
rape-of-lucrece-l722: She says, her subjects with foul insurrection
rape-of-lucrece-l723: Have batter’d down her consecrated wall,
rape-of-lucrece-l724: And by their mortal fault brought in subjection
rape-of-lucrece-l725: Her immortality, and made her thrall
rape-of-lucrece-l726: To living death and pain perpetual:
rape-of-lucrece-l727: Which in her prescience she controlled still,
rape-of-lucrece-l728: But her foresight could not forestall their will.
rape-of-lucrece-l729: Even in this thought through the dark night he stealeth,
rape-of-lucrece-l730: A captive victor that hath lost in gain;
rape-of-lucrece-l731: Bearing away the wound that nothing healeth,
rape-of-lucrece-l732: The scar that will, despite of cure, remain;
rape-of-lucrece-l733: Leaving his spoil perplex’d in greater pain.
rape-of-lucrece-l734: She hears the load of lust he left behind,
rape-of-lucrece-l735: And he the burthen of a guilty mind.
rape-of-lucrece-l736: He like a thievish dog creeps sadly thence;
rape-of-lucrece-l737: She like a wearied lamb lies panting there;
rape-of-lucrece-l738: He scowls and hates himself for his offence;
rape-of-lucrece-l739: She, desperate, with her nails her flesh doth tear;
rape-of-lucrece-l740: He faintly flies, sweating with guilty fear;
rape-of-lucrece-l741: She stays, exclaiming on the direful night;
rape-of-lucrece-l742: He runs, and chides his vanish’d, loathed delight.
rape-of-lucrece-l743: He thence departs a heavy convertite;
rape-of-lucrece-l744: She there remains a hopeless castaway;
rape-of-lucrece-l745: He in his speed looks for the morning light;
rape-of-lucrece-l746: She prays she never may behold the day,
rape-of-lucrece-l747: “For day,” quoth she, “night’s scapes doth open lay,
rape-of-lucrece-l748: And my true eyes have never practised how
rape-of-lucrece-l749: To cloak offences with a cunning brow.
rape-of-lucrece-l750: “They think not but that every eye can see
rape-of-lucrece-l751: The same disgrace which they themselves behold;
rape-of-lucrece-l752: And therefore would they still in darkness be,
rape-of-lucrece-l753: To have their unseen sin remain untold;
rape-of-lucrece-l754: For they their guilt with weeping will unfold,
rape-of-lucrece-l755: And grave, like water that doth eat in steel,
rape-of-lucrece-l756: Upon my cheeks what helpless shame I feel.”
rape-of-lucrece-l757: Here she exclaims against repose and rest,
rape-of-lucrece-l758: And bids her eyes hereafter still be blind.
rape-of-lucrece-l759: She wakes her heart by beating on her breast,
rape-of-lucrece-l760: And bids it leap from thence, where it may find
rape-of-lucrece-l761: Some purer chest to close so pure a mind.
rape-of-lucrece-l762: Frantic with grief thus breathes she forth her spite
rape-of-lucrece-l763: Against the unseen secrecy of night:
rape-of-lucrece-l765: Dim register and notary of shame!
rape-of-lucrece-l766: Black stage for tragedies and murders fell!
rape-of-lucrece-l767: Vast sin-concealing chaos! nurse of blame!
rape-of-lucrece-l768: Blind muffled bawd! dark harbour for defame!
rape-of-lucrece-l769: Grim cave of death! whispering conspirator
rape-of-lucrece-l770: With close-tongued treason and the ravisher!
rape-of-lucrece-l772: Since thou art guilty of my cureless crime,
rape-of-lucrece-l773: Muster thy mists to meet the eastern light,
rape-of-lucrece-l774: Make war against proportion’d course of time;
rape-of-lucrece-l775: Or if thou wilt permit the sun to climb
rape-of-lucrece-l776: His wonted height, yet ere he go to bed,
rape-of-lucrece-l777: Knit poisonous clouds about his golden head.
rape-of-lucrece-l778: “With rotten damps ravish the morning air;
rape-of-lucrece-l779: Let their exhaled unwholesome breaths make sick
rape-of-lucrece-l780: The life of purity, the supreme fair,
rape-of-lucrece-l781: Ere he arrive his weary noon-tide prick;
rape-of-lucrece-l782: And let thy misty vapours march so thick,
rape-of-lucrece-l783: That in their smoky ranks his smother’d light
rape-of-lucrece-l784: May set at noon and make perpetual night.
rape-of-lucrece-l785: “Were Tarquin Night, as he is but Night’s child,
rape-of-lucrece-l786: The silver-shining queen he would distain;
rape-of-lucrece-l787: Her twinkling handmaids too, by him defiled,
rape-of-lucrece-l788: Through Night’s black bosom should not peep again:
rape-of-lucrece-l789: So should I have co-partners in my pain;
rape-of-lucrece-l790: And fellowship in woe doth woe assuage,
rape-of-lucrece-l791: As palmers’ chat makes short their pilgrimage.
rape-of-lucrece-l792: “Where now I have no one to blush with me,
rape-of-lucrece-l793: To cross their arms and hang their heads with mine,
rape-of-lucrece-l794: To mask their brows and hide their infamy;
rape-of-lucrece-l795: But I alone alone must sit and pine,
rape-of-lucrece-l796: Seasoning the earth with showers of silver brine,
rape-of-lucrece-l797: Mingling my talk with tears, my grief with groans,
rape-of-lucrece-l798: Poor wasting monuments of lasting moans.
rape-of-lucrece-l799: “O Night, thou furnace of foul-reeking smoke,
rape-of-lucrece-l800: Let not the jealous Day behold that face
rape-of-lucrece-l801: Which underneath thy black all-hiding cloak
rape-of-lucrece-l803: Keep still possession of thy gloomy place,
rape-of-lucrece-l804: That all the faults which in thy reign are made
rape-of-lucrece-l805: May likewise be sepulchred in thy shade!
rape-of-lucrece-l806: “Make me not object to the tell-tale Day!
rape-of-lucrece-l807: The light will show, character’d in my brow,
rape-of-lucrece-l808: The story of sweet chastity’s decay,
rape-of-lucrece-l809: The impious breach of holy wedlock vow:
rape-of-lucrece-l810: Yea, the illiterate, that know not how
rape-of-lucrece-l811: To cipher what is writ in learned books,
rape-of-lucrece-l812: Will quote my loathsome trespass in my looks.
rape-of-lucrece-l813: “The nurse, to still her child, will tell my story,
rape-of-lucrece-l814: And fright her crying babe with Tarquin’s name;
rape-of-lucrece-l815: The orator, to deck his oratory,
rape-of-lucrece-l816: Will couple my reproach to Tarquin’s shame;
rape-of-lucrece-l818: Will tie the hearers to attend each line,
rape-of-lucrece-l819: How Tarquin wronged me, I Collatine.
rape-of-lucrece-l820: “Let my good name, that senseless reputation,
rape-of-lucrece-l821: For Collatine’s dear love be kept unspotted:
rape-of-lucrece-l822: If that be made a theme for disputation,
rape-of-lucrece-l823: The branches of another root are rotted,
rape-of-lucrece-l824: And undeserved reproach to him allotted
rape-of-lucrece-l825: That is as clear from this attaint of mine
rape-of-lucrece-l826: As I, ere this, was pure to Collatine.
rape-of-lucrece-l828: O unfelt sore! crest-wounding, private scar!
rape-of-lucrece-l829: Reproach is stamp’d in Collatinus’ face,
rape-of-lucrece-l830: And Tarquin’s eye may read the mot afar,
rape-of-lucrece-l831: How he in peace is wounded, not in war.
rape-of-lucrece-l832: Alas, how many bear such shameful blows,
rape-of-lucrece-l833: Which not themselves, but he that gives them knows!
rape-of-lucrece-l834: “If, Collatine, thine honour lay in me,
rape-of-lucrece-l835: From me by strong assault it is bereft.
rape-of-lucrece-l836: My honey lost, and I, a drone-like bee,
rape-of-lucrece-l837: Have no perfection of my summer left,
rape-of-lucrece-l838: But robb’d and ransack’d by injurious theft:
rape-of-lucrece-l839: In thy weak hive a wandering wasp hath crept,
rape-of-lucrece-l840: And suck’d the honey which thy chaste bee kept.
rape-of-lucrece-l841: “Yet am I guilty of thy honour’s wrack;
rape-of-lucrece-l842: Yet for thy honour did I entertain him;
rape-of-lucrece-l843: Coming from thee, I could not put him back,
rape-of-lucrece-l844: For it had been dishonour to disdain him:
rape-of-lucrece-l845: Besides, of weariness he did complain him,
rape-of-lucrece-l846: And talk’d of virtue: O unlook’d-for evil,
rape-of-lucrece-l847: When virtue is profaned in such a devil!
rape-of-lucrece-l848: “Why should the worm intrude the maiden bud?
rape-of-lucrece-l849: Or hateful cuckoos hatch in sparrows’ nests?
rape-of-lucrece-l850: Or toads infect fair founts with venom mud?
rape-of-lucrece-l851: Or tyrant folly lurk in gentle breasts?
rape-of-lucrece-l852: Or kings be breakers of their own behests?
rape-of-lucrece-l853: But no perfection is so absolute,
rape-of-lucrece-l854: That some impurity doth not pollute.
rape-of-lucrece-l855: “The aged man that coffers-up his gold
rape-of-lucrece-l856: Is plagued with cramps and gouts and painful fits;
rape-of-lucrece-l857: And scarce hath eyes his treasure to behold,
rape-of-lucrece-l858: But like still-pining Tantalus he sits,
rape-of-lucrece-l859: And useless barns the harvest of his wits;
rape-of-lucrece-l860: Having no other pleasure of his gain
rape-of-lucrece-l861: But torment that it cannot cure his pain.
rape-of-lucrece-l862: “So then he hath it when he cannot use it,
rape-of-lucrece-l863: And leaves it to be master’d by his young;
rape-of-lucrece-l864: Who in their pride do presently abuse it:
rape-of-lucrece-l865: Their father was too weak, and they too strong,
rape-of-lucrece-l866: To hold their cursed-blessed fortune long.
rape-of-lucrece-l867: The sweets we wish for turn to loathed sours
rape-of-lucrece-l868: Even in the moment that we call them ours.
rape-of-lucrece-l869: “Unruly blasts wait on the tender spring;
rape-of-lucrece-l870: Unwholesome weeds take root with precious flowers;
rape-of-lucrece-l871: The adder hisses where the sweet birds sing;
rape-of-lucrece-l873: We have no good that we can say is ours,
rape-of-lucrece-l875: Or kills his life or else his quality.
rape-of-lucrece-l877: ’Tis thou that executest the traitor’s treason:
rape-of-lucrece-l878: Thou set’st the wolf where he the lamb may get;
rape-of-lucrece-l879: Whoever plots the sin, thou ’point’st the season;
rape-of-lucrece-l880: ’Tis thou that spurn’st at right, at law, at reason;
rape-of-lucrece-l881: And in thy shady cell, where none may spy him,
rape-of-lucrece-l882: Sits Sin, to seize the souls that wander by him.
rape-of-lucrece-l883: “Thou makest the vestal violate her oath;
rape-of-lucrece-l884: Thou blow’st the fire when temperance is thaw’d;
rape-of-lucrece-l885: Thou smother’st honesty, thou murder’st troth;
rape-of-lucrece-l886: Thou foul abettor! thou notorious bawd!
rape-of-lucrece-l887: Thou plantest scandal and displacest laud:
rape-of-lucrece-l888: Thou ravisher, thou traitor, thou false thief,
rape-of-lucrece-l889: Thy honey turns to gall, thy joy to grief!
rape-of-lucrece-l890: “Thy secret pleasure turns to open shame,
rape-of-lucrece-l891: Thy private feasting to a public fast,
rape-of-lucrece-l892: Thy smoothing titles to a ragged name,
rape-of-lucrece-l893: Thy sugar’d tongue to bitter wormwood taste:
rape-of-lucrece-l894: Thy violent vanities can never last.
rape-of-lucrece-l895: How comes it then, vile Opportunity,
rape-of-lucrece-l896: Being so bad, such numbers seek for thee?
rape-of-lucrece-l897: “When wilt thou be the humble suppliant’s friend,
rape-of-lucrece-l898: And bring him where his suit may be obtain’d?
rape-of-lucrece-l899: When wilt thou sort an hour great strifes to end?
rape-of-lucrece-l900: Or free that soul which wretchedness hath chain’d?
rape-of-lucrece-l901: Give physic to the sick, ease to the pain’d?
rape-of-lucrece-l902: The poor, lame, blind, halt, creep, cry out for thee;
rape-of-lucrece-l903: But they ne’er meet with Opportunity.
rape-of-lucrece-l904: “The patient dies while the physician sleeps;
rape-of-lucrece-l905: The orphan pines while the oppressor feeds;
rape-of-lucrece-l906: Justice is feasting while the widow weeps;
rape-of-lucrece-l907: Advice is sporting while infection breeds:
rape-of-lucrece-l908: Thou grant’st no time for charitable deeds:
rape-of-lucrece-l909: Wrath, envy, treason, rape, and murder’s rages,
rape-of-lucrece-l910: Thy heinous hours wait on them as their pages.
rape-of-lucrece-l911: “When Truth and Virtue have to do with thee,
rape-of-lucrece-l912: A thousand crosses keep them from thy aid:
rape-of-lucrece-l913: They buy thy help; but Sin ne’er gives a fee,
rape-of-lucrece-l914: He gratis comes; and thou art well appaid
rape-of-lucrece-l915: As well to hear as grant what he hath said.
rape-of-lucrece-l916: My Collatine would else have come to me
rape-of-lucrece-l917: When Tarquin did, but he was stay’d by thee.
rape-of-lucrece-l918: “Guilty thou art of murder and of theft,
rape-of-lucrece-l920: Guilty of treason, forgery, and shift,
rape-of-lucrece-l923: To all sins past, and all that are to come,
rape-of-lucrece-l924: From the creation to the general doom.
rape-of-lucrece-l926: Swift subtle post, carrier of grisly care,
rape-of-lucrece-l927: Eater of youth, false slave to false delight,
rape-of-lucrece-l928: Base watch of woes, sin’s pack-horse, virtue’s snare;
rape-of-lucrece-l929: Thou nursest all and murder’st all that are:
rape-of-lucrece-l930: O, hear me then, injurious, shifting Time!
rape-of-lucrece-l931: Be guilty of my death, since of my crime.
rape-of-lucrece-l933: Betray’d the hours thou gavest me to repose,
rape-of-lucrece-l934: Cancell’d my fortunes, and enchained me
rape-of-lucrece-l935: To endless date of never-ending woes?
rape-of-lucrece-l936: Time’s office is to fine the hate of foes;
rape-of-lucrece-l937: To eat up errors by opinion bred,
rape-of-lucrece-l938: Not spend the dowry of a lawful bed.
rape-of-lucrece-l939: “Time’s glory is to calm contending kings,
rape-of-lucrece-l940: To unmask falsehood and bring truth to light,
rape-of-lucrece-l941: To stamp the seal of time in aged things,
rape-of-lucrece-l942: To wake the morn and sentinel the night,
rape-of-lucrece-l943: To wrong the wronger till he render right,
rape-of-lucrece-l944: To ruinate proud buildings with thy hours,
rape-of-lucrece-l945: And smear with dust their glittering golden towers;
rape-of-lucrece-l947: To feed oblivion with decay of things,
rape-of-lucrece-l948: To blot old books and alter their contents,
rape-of-lucrece-l949: To pluck the quills from ancient ravens’ wings,
rape-of-lucrece-l950: To dry the old oak’s sap and cherish springs,
rape-of-lucrece-l951: To spoil antiquities of hammer’d steel,
rape-of-lucrece-l952: And turn the giddy round of Fortune’s wheel;
rape-of-lucrece-l953: “To show the beldam daughters of her daughter,
rape-of-lucrece-l954: To make the child a man, the man a child,
rape-of-lucrece-l955: To slay the tiger that doth live by slaughter,
rape-of-lucrece-l956: To tame the unicorn and lion wild,
rape-of-lucrece-l957: To mock the subtle in themselves beguiled,
rape-of-lucrece-l958: To cheer the ploughman with increaseful crops,
rape-of-lucrece-l959: And waste huge stones with little water-drops.
rape-of-lucrece-l960: “Why work’st thou mischief in thy pilgrimage,
rape-of-lucrece-l961: Unless thou couldst return to make amends?
rape-of-lucrece-l962: One poor retiring minute in an age
rape-of-lucrece-l963: Would purchase thee a thousand thousand friends,
rape-of-lucrece-l964: Lending him wit that to bad debtors lends:
rape-of-lucrece-l965: O, this dread night, wouldst thou one hour come back,
rape-of-lucrece-l966: I could prevent this storm and shun thy wrack!
rape-of-lucrece-l968: With some mischance cross Tarquin in his flight:
rape-of-lucrece-l970: To make him curse this cursed crimeful night:
rape-of-lucrece-l971: Let ghastly shadows his lewd eyes affright;
rape-of-lucrece-l972: And the dire thought of his committed evil
rape-of-lucrece-l973: Shape every bush a hideous shapeless devil.
rape-of-lucrece-l974: “Disturb his hours of rest with restless trances,
rape-of-lucrece-l975: Afflict him in his bed with bedrid groans;
rape-of-lucrece-l976: Let there bechance him pitiful mischances,
rape-of-lucrece-l977: To make him moan; but pity not his moans:
rape-of-lucrece-l978: Stone him with harden’d hearts, harder than stones;
rape-of-lucrece-l979: And let mild women to him lose their mildness,
rape-of-lucrece-l980: Wilder to him than tigers in their wildness.
rape-of-lucrece-l981: “Let him have time to tear his curled hair,
rape-of-lucrece-l982: Let him have time against himself to rave,
rape-of-lucrece-l983: Let him have time of Time’s help to despair,
rape-of-lucrece-l984: Let him have time to live a loathed slave,
rape-of-lucrece-l985: Let him have time a beggar’s orts to crave,
rape-of-lucrece-l986: And time to see one that by alms doth live
rape-of-lucrece-l987: Disdain to him disdained scraps to give.
rape-of-lucrece-l988: “Let him have time to see his friends his foes,
rape-of-lucrece-l989: And merry fools to mock at him resort;
rape-of-lucrece-l990: Let him have time to mark how slow time goes
rape-of-lucrece-l991: In time of sorrow, and how swift and short
rape-of-lucrece-l992: His time of folly and his time of sport;
rape-of-lucrece-l993: And ever let his unrecalling crime
rape-of-lucrece-l994: Have time to wail th’ abusing of his time.
rape-of-lucrece-l995: “O Time, thou tutor both to good and bad,
rape-of-lucrece-l996: Teach me to curse him that thou taught’st this ill!
rape-of-lucrece-l997: At his own shadow let the thief run mad,
rape-of-lucrece-l998: Himself himself seek every hour to kill!
rape-of-lucrece-l999: Such wretched hands such wretched blood should spill;
rape-of-lucrece-l1000: For who so base would such an office have
rape-of-lucrece-l1001: As slanderous deathsman to so base a slave?
rape-of-lucrece-l1002: The baser is he, coming from a king,
rape-of-lucrece-l1003: To shame his hope with deeds degenerate:
rape-of-lucrece-l1004: The mightier man, the mightier is the thing
rape-of-lucrece-l1005: That makes him honour’d, or begets him hate;
rape-of-lucrece-l1006: For greatest scandal waits on greatest state.
rape-of-lucrece-l1007: The moon being clouded presently is miss’d,
rape-of-lucrece-l1008: But little stars may hide them when they list.
rape-of-lucrece-l1009: “The crow may bathe his coal-black wings in mire,
rape-of-lucrece-l1010: And unperceived fly with the filth away;
rape-of-lucrece-l1011: But if the like the snow-white swan desire,
rape-of-lucrece-l1012: The stain upon his silver down will stay.
rape-of-lucrece-l1013: Poor grooms are sightless night, kings glorious day:
rape-of-lucrece-l1014: Gnats are unnoted wheresoe’er they fly,
rape-of-lucrece-l1015: But eagles gazed upon with every eye.
rape-of-lucrece-l1016: “Out, idle words, servants to shallow fools!
rape-of-lucrece-l1019: Debate where leisure serves with dull debaters;
rape-of-lucrece-l1020: To trembling clients be you mediators:
rape-of-lucrece-l1021: For me, I force not argument a straw,
rape-of-lucrece-l1022: Since that my case is past the help of law.
rape-of-lucrece-l1024: At Time, at Tarquin, and uncheerful Night;
rape-of-lucrece-l1025: In vain I cavil with mine infamy,
rape-of-lucrece-l1026: In vain I spurn at my confirm’d despite:
rape-of-lucrece-l1027: This helpless smoke of words doth me no right.
rape-of-lucrece-l1028: The remedy indeed to do me good
rape-of-lucrece-l1029: Is to let forth my foul-defiled blood.
rape-of-lucrece-l1030: “Poor hand, why quiver’st thou at this decree?
rape-of-lucrece-l1031: Honour thyself to rid me of this shame;
rape-of-lucrece-l1032: For if I die, my honour lives in thee;
rape-of-lucrece-l1033: But if I live, thou livest in my defame:
rape-of-lucrece-l1034: Since thou couldst not defend thy loyal dame,
rape-of-lucrece-l1035: And wast afeard to scratch her wicked foe,
rape-of-lucrece-l1036: Kill both thyself and her for yielding so.”
rape-of-lucrece-l1037: This said, from her be-tumbled couch she starteth,
rape-of-lucrece-l1038: To find some desperate instrument of death:
rape-of-lucrece-l1039: But this no slaughterhouse no tool imparteth
rape-of-lucrece-l1040: To make more vent for passage of her breath;
rape-of-lucrece-l1041: Which, thronging through her lips, so vanisheth
rape-of-lucrece-l1042: As smoke from Aetna, that in air consumes,
rape-of-lucrece-l1043: Or that which from discharged cannon fumes.
rape-of-lucrece-l1044: “In vain,” quoth she, “I live, and seek in vain
rape-of-lucrece-l1045: Some happy mean to end a hapless life.
rape-of-lucrece-l1046: I fear’d by Tarquin’s falchion to be slain,
rape-of-lucrece-l1047: Yet for the self-same purpose seek a knife:
rape-of-lucrece-l1048: But when I fear’d I was a loyal wife:
rape-of-lucrece-l1049: So am I now: O no, that cannot be;
rape-of-lucrece-l1050: Of that true type hath Tarquin rifled me.
